title: O, May Our Sympathizing Breasts
description: O, May Our Sympathizing Breasts in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 382 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, may our sym-pa-thiz-ing breasts The gen-erous plea-sure know, Kind-ly to share in o-thers' joy, And weep for o-thers' woe!

lines: Kindly to share in others' joy,
Where'er the helpless sons of grief
Soft be our hearts their pains to feel,
And swift our hands to aid.
O, be the law of love fulfilled
Be thou, my heart, dilated wide
And, in one grasp of fervent love,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
